Compute marginal discovery rate and saturation

marginal_saturation.Rd

Computes the marginal discovery rate (the instantaneous slope of the discovery curve, i.e., expected new nodes and edges discovered per additional sequencing read) and the corresponding marginal (Good-Turing) saturation at full sequencing depth for each component in a PixelDB object.

Usage

marginal_saturation(db, components = NULL, table_name = NULL, min_degree = 1L)

Arguments

db

A PixelDB object with an active DuckDB connection.

components

Optional character vector of component names to include. If NULL (default), all components are included.

table_name

Optional name for materializing the result as a table in the DuckDB connection.

min_degree

Integer (1L or 2L); minimum node degree at the current depth for a node to be counted. Default is 1L (all nodes). Set to 2L to measure the discovery rate of dynamic degree >= 2 core nodes.

Value

A lazy tbl (DuckDB query) with columns:

component

The component (cell) identifier.

read_count

Total sequencing reads in the component.

nodes

Number of unique nodes (with degree >= min_degree).

edges

Number of unique edges in the component.

degree

Average node degree (\(2 \times \text{edges} / \text{nodes}\)).

node_discovery_rate

Instantaneous slope \(dN / dR\) (new nodes per additional read).

edge_discovery_rate

Instantaneous slope \(dE / dR\) (new edges per additional read).

degree_rate

Instantaneous slope \(d\bar{d} / dR\) (change in average node degree per additional read).

marginal_node_saturation

Marginal node saturation (\(1 - (dN / dR) / 2\)).

marginal_edge_saturation

Marginal (Good-Turing) edge saturation (\(1 - dE / dR\)).

Details

Marginal discovery rate (slope)

Let \(\mathbb{E}[U(p)]\) be the expected number of unique elements (nodes or edges) observed at downsampling fraction \(p \in (0, 1]\), and let \(R(p) = p R\) be the downsampled read count. The instantaneous slope of the discovery curve with respect to sequencing reads is: $$\frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[U(p)]}{dR(p)} = \frac{1}{R} \frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[U(p)]}{dp}$$

Evaluated at full sequencing depth (\(p = 1\)):

  • Edges: An edge with \(r_e\) reads has retention probability \(1 - (1 - p)^{r_e}\), whose derivative at \(p = 1\) is \(1\) if \(r_e = 1\) and \(0\) if \(r_e \ge 2\). Thus, the edge discovery rate at full depth is the fraction of reads supporting singleton edges (\(E_1\)): $$\text{edge\_discovery\_rate} = \left.\frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[E]}{dR}\right|_{p=1} = \frac{E_1}{R}$$

  • Nodes (min_degree = 1): A node with total incident reads \(r_v\) has retention probability \(1 - (1 - p)^{r_v}\), so at \(p = 1\): $$\text{node\_discovery\_rate} = \left.\frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[N]}{dR}\right|_{p=1} = \frac{N_1}{R}$$ where \(N_1\) is the number of singleton nodes (\(r_v = 1\)).

  • Core nodes (min_degree = 2): A node is in the dynamic 2-core at fraction \(p\) if at least two of its incident edges are retained: $$P(\text{deg}_v(p) \ge 2) = 1 + (d_v - 1)(1 - p)^{r_v} - \sum_{e \ni v} (1 - p)^{r_v - r_e}$$ Taking the derivative with respect to \(p\) at \(p = 1\), the only terms with \(r_v - r_e = 1\) occur when a degree-2 node (\(d_v = 2\)) has an incident singleton edge (\(r_e = 1\)), so: $$\text{node\_discovery\_rate} = \left.\frac{d\,\mathbb{E}[N_{\text{deg} \ge 2}]}{dR}\right|_{p=1} = \frac{\sum_{v:\, d_v = 2} s_v}{R}$$ where \(s_v \in \{0, 1, 2\}\) is the number of incident singleton edges on degree-2 node \(v\).

Multiplying node_discovery_rate or edge_discovery_rate by 10000 gives the expected number of new unique nodes or edges gained per 10,000 additional sequencing reads.

Marginal (Good-Turing) saturation

The marginal saturation is the probability that the next observation lands on an already-observed element rather than discovering a new one (since each sequencing read observes 2 node endpoints, node_discovery_rate is divided by 2): $$S_{\text{marginal, edge}} = 1 - \text{edge\_discovery\_rate}$$ $$S_{\text{marginal, node}} = 1 - \frac{\text{node\_discovery\_rate}}{2}$$

The instantaneous rate of change of average node degree (\(\bar{d} = 2E / N\)) per additional read is given by the quotient rule: $$\text{degree\_rate} = \frac{d\bar{d}}{dR} = \frac{2\,\text{edge\_discovery\_rate} - \bar{d}\,\text{node\_discovery\_rate}}{N}$$

See also

marginal_saturation_curve for computing marginal discovery rates and saturation across downsampling fractions. approximate_node_saturation and approximate_edge_saturation for cumulative saturation.
